title: Eval-driven contracts and staged launch playbook for hosted mixed endpoints (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank)
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Purpose: create a concise PRD and operational playbook to launch a combined hosted API surface that includes chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints using eval-driven behavioral contracts and a staged rollout. The emphasis is on measurable acceptance (eval suites + telemetry), graded fallback policies, and minimal customer disruption while preserving unit-cost targets.

This ticket captures acceptance criteria, scope decisions, rollout phases, required telemetry/dashboards, and a lightweight incident/runbook template for rollbacks.
background: The product team needs a single playbook for mixed endpoint launches that focuses on behavioral correctness (not just API compatibility) because past launches saw regressions in qa suites after kernel/kernel-selection changes. The runtime team is shipping batching and kernel improvements that may change output characteristics; we must gate launch on eval performance and operational signals.
goals: 1) Define acceptance contracts per endpoint that combine functional evals and non-functional SLOs (latency/cost). 2) Provide a staged rollout plan with traffic buckets and automated rollback criteria. 3) Ensure observability + eval runs are integrated into CI and the Console readiness dashboard. 4) Keep the minimal viable rollback path to a pinned model variant and hosted fallback lane.
scope_in_scope:
- PRD-level behavioral contracts for chat, completions, embeddings, rerank.
- A canonical eval suite per endpoint (prompt sets + scoring harness).
- Acceptance thresholds and regression tolerances.
- Staged rollout plan with canary -> ramp -> global.
- Telemetry collection and dashboards.
- Runbook for rollback/mitigation.
- Documentation pointers for SDK/contract changes.
scope_out_of_scope:
- New model training or model architecture changes.
- Deep UX work in Console (we'll add a single readiness dashboard tile).
- Major pricing changes or billing integration.
- On-prem/private deployment integration (covered in a separate PRD).
acceptance_criteria: Functional: Each endpoint passes its eval suite at defined thresholds (chat: 90% pass on core intent prompts; completions: BLEU/ROUGE targets agreed in eval doc; embeddings: mean cosine > 0.78 on curated similarity pairs; rerank: NDCG@5 delta <= 0.02 vs baseline).
Latency: P50 and P95 for each endpoint must meet target lanes (chat P95 <= 350ms for short prompts; embeddings P95 <= 120ms).
Cost: Unit token cost must not exceed the target by more than 12% for the canary lane; optimization suggestions required if exceeded.
Observability: Console dashboard shows per-model/token cost, per-route latency distribution, error rate, and eval regression alerts. All charts must be green in the readiness checklist.
Fallbacks: Canary must include an automated fallback to a pinned model variant or regional replica if error rate > 1% or eval regression triggered. Fallback automation tested in staging.
CI gating: Pull requests that change kernel selection or quantization must run the relevant eval suites in CI; PR cannot merge without tests passing and an analyst sign-off.
Documentation: Public API surface changes, behavioral notes, and migration guidance published to docs.redwood.ai and linked from SDK changelog.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Pre-launch: Run full eval suite against staging models. Bootstrapping: create canonical prompt sets, golden references, and scoring scripts. Validate console telemetry. (owner: PM + ENG infra).

Phase 1 - Canary (1% traffic): Route 1% of new traffic to canary lane for 48h. Continuous evals run on sampled outputs; daily manual review of flagged regressions by PM + Research. Automated rollback triggers on threshold breaches.
Phase 2 - Ramp (1% -> 25% over 7 days): Expand if no major regressions. Monitor cost per-token and latency SLOs. Execute additional targeted prompt sweeps for higher-risk customers.
Phase 3 - Regional Expansion (25% -> 75%): Ramp regionally while watching region-specific latency and error signals. Activate increased KV cache warmth windows.
Phase 4 - Global Launch (75% -> 100%): Final ramp if all metrics stable for 72h. Post-launch, schedule weekly eval runs for 4 weeks to catch slow regressions.
telemetry_requirements: Per-route latency histograms (P50/P90/P95) and tail analysis by sequence length.
Error rate and class breakdown (timeouts, OOM, model failures).
Sampled output archival for eval re-scoring and triage (7d retention for canary; 30d for ramp lanes).
Automated eval regression alerts tied to a runbook with ownership mapped.
tradeoffs_and_decisions:
- Decision: require eval gating in CI for kernel/quantization changes to prevent silent regressions (tradeoff: longer CI time vs safer launches).
- Tradeoff: tighter cost ceiling reduces model options; we prioritize behavioral fidelity for Tier-1 customers and a cost-aware fallback lane for low-cost routing.
- Decision: keep embeddings evaluation to curated semantic tests over production-sampled pairs to reduce noise in early stages.
- Decision: do not delay launch for minor latency variance if functional evals pass and fallback automation exists.
risks:
- Eval coverage blind spots: prompts not representative of customer workloads. Mitigation: invite 3 customers to contribute prompt sets to the canonical suite.
- CI flakiness on GPU tests: mitigation is to isolate eval runs to deterministic CPU-mode scoring where possible and mark flaky tests.
- Unexpected cost spike during ramp: mitigation is an automated cap on unit cost routing and a rapid pause control in Console.
runbook_summary: When a regression alert fires: 1) Pause ramp and switch traffic to pinned baseline. 2) Capture 10k sampled requests and run offline eval re-scoring. 3) Triage in 2-hour war-room with PM/ENG/Research. 4) Decide rollback or patch; communicate to affected customers. 5) Postmortem within 7 days.
